metadata_sample.rules_text:
- If sentiment is consistently neutral or negative (0.00), model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope or add early mean-reversion term.
- When sentiment shows minor positive signals (e.g., 0.20–0.33), model should not overreact; cap forecast growth to avoid overestimating bullish momentum.
- If history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline), model should not assume continuation; adjust forecast toward historical mean or recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >15% from 14-day moving average, consider adding sentiment-weighted smoothing or lagged sentiment correction.
- If sentiment history includes multiple 0.20–0.40 spikes, model should not assume sustained rally; apply diminishing returns or exponential decay to forecast growth.
